segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
This is a night for when you have lost someone. [pause 10]

You do not have to do anything here. You can lie down, or stay just as you are, with the phone in the dark beside you. [pause 12]

Tonight we read Psalm 13. It is short, and it is honest. David asks God the same question four times. How long. [pause 12]

We will read it twice, slowly. [pause 12]

verses.text: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?
Consider and hear me, O LORD my God: lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death;
Lest mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him; and those that trouble me rejoice when I am moved.
But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.
I will sing unto the LORD, because he hath dealt bountifully with me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
How long. That question is in the Bible. Someone prayed it out loud, and God let it be written down. [pause 14]

Grief can feel as if God has gone quiet. The psalm does not scold David for saying so. It lets him say it. [pause 14]

You can say it too. Out loud, or only in your heart. Your questions do not offend God. [pause 15]

Then, near the end, David says one small word. But. He trusts God's mercy while the question is still open. [pause 15]

Here are two short passages to sit beside it. [pause 12]

verses.text: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Jesus wept. He stood with Mary and Martha in their sorrow, and he cried too. [pause 15]

And the psalmist pictures God keeping every tear in a bottle. Not one is wasted. Not one is forgotten. [pause 15]

Whoever you are missing tonight, you can bring their name to God. You do not have to find the right words. [pause 15]

Now Psalm 13 once more. If a line is yours tonight, let it be yours. [pause 15]

verses.text: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?
Consider and hear me, O LORD my God: lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death;
Lest mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him; and those that trouble me rejoice when I am moved.
But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.
I will sing unto the LORD, because he hath dealt bountifully with me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will stop reading now. [pause 8]

Let the room be quiet. Let your breathing find its own pace. [pause 12]

There is nothing you need to fix tonight, and nothing you are supposed to feel. [pause 12]

If the tears come, let them come. If they do not, that is all right too. [pause 15]

The love you have for them is still here. It does not have to go anywhere. [pause 15]

If the nights stay this heavy, talk with your pastor, or with a grief counselor. Nobody is meant to carry this alone. [pause 15]

The Lord is near to the broken in heart. Stay here as long as you need. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Grief nights and the 3 AM night (21 Nov 2026): every passage is stored KJV pasted by code (Ps 13, Ps 23, John 11:32-36, Ps 4:8 and companions); written lines echo in short phrases only. Lament is allowed (How long) without rebuke; no reason given for a death, no 'better place', no timeline for grief (the grief_words check); Rev 21:4 told as the hope at the end of the story, not a claim about the person who died; Jesus's and God's words given indirectly outside scripture. Each grief night points to a pastor or a grief counselor; the 3 AM night makes no sleep promise.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a grieving or half-awake listener can follow at 3 AM; the person who died is 'them', never assumed to be a spouse, parent or child; no pity, no hurry ('nobody is timing you'); the 3 AM night is short and spare, the phone face down. Lengths by silence only: grief nights 10-11.5 min, the 3 AM night 6 min (estimated at 117 wpm).
